articles.title: New AI-Managed ETFs Remove Human Stock Pickers Entirely. Here’s What That Means
articles.query: site:forbes.com "artificial intelligence" (trading OR "stock market" OR portfolio OR "hedge fund")
articles.text:
In 2017, an ETF called AIEQ launched with a bold premise: Let artificial intelligence, powered by IBM’s Watson, pick stocks. It was among the first funds to hand the core of its investment process to a machine. Eight years later, AIEQ has provided a real-world stress test for the concept and the results have been humbling. The fund has trailed the S&P 500 for much of its existence, delivering roughly half the cumulative return of a simple index fund over comparable periods.
Finq , an AI-focused fintech firm backed by Palo Alto Networks founder and billionaire Nir Zuk, has launched two actively managed ETFs — AIUP and AINT — that it describes as “the first SEC-registered funds managed entirely by AI.” Unlike earlier AI-powered funds where human portfolio managers retained the ability to override the machine’s recommendations, Finq says its AI framework handles all stock selection, weighting, and rebalancing. Humans oversee the system’s governance and regulatory compliance, but they do not interfere with individual investment decisions.
“AI in the investment world has the capacity to outperform humans,” said Eldad Tamir, Finq’s founder and CEO, in the company’s press release . “Finq is built on a data-only system that makes investment decisions without the disadvantages aligned with human fear, greed, urgency to act and other disabling human attributes.”
It’s a confident thesis. But if history is any guide, confidence alone hasn’t been enough.
Finq’s structural argument, though, is worth examining on its terms. Most funds that describe themselves as “AI-powered” use machine learning as a research tool — scanning sentiment data, processing earnings reports and flagging patterns.
The final call still rests with a human portfolio manager. AIEQ’s prospectus, for instance, notes that its managers may exercise discretion alongside AI’s recommendations.
Finq draws a sharper line. Its proprietary model produces a daily relative ranking of every stock in the S&P 500. AIUP takes long positions in the highest-ranked names. AINT pairs long positions in top-ranked stocks with short positions in the lowest-ranked, maintaining a dollar-neutral posture designed to profit from relative performance rather than overall market direction. The long/short structure, in particular, brings a hedge fund-like strategy into a retail-accessible ETF wrapper — something that is genuinely uncommon at this price point.
The involvement of Zuk also adds a different dimension. Zuk, whose cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks commands a market capitalization north of $125 billion, has been a longtime backer of Finq, injecting $6 million into the company in 2023.
He built that fortune on a core bet that automated systems could identify network threats faster and more reliably than human analysts. Finq is making the same bet about financial markets — that pattern recognition at machine speed, stripped of human emotion, can find value that traditional managers miss.
A report from the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator, found that funds using AI in their investment process showed no significant performance advantage over non-AI funds since 2022, whether measured by average returns or risk-adjusted returns. The finding held even when researchers controlled for fund size, age, and geographic focus.
Another study examining AI-driven investment funds in the U.S. painted an even starker picture: All 11 funds fully reliant on artificial intelligence — with no human intervention — underperformed the S&P 500. Six of them posted outright losses during what was otherwise a bullish market. The average annual return across those fully autonomous funds was negative 1.8%.
However, it’s worth noting that this performance gap isn’t unique to AI. The S&P Indices Versus Active (SPIVA) Mid-Year 2025 Scorecard found that only about 14% of actively managed U.S. large-cap funds beat the S&P 500 over a ten-year window.
Bryan Armour, director of ETF and passive strategies research at Morningstar, noted that just 33% of active strategies outperformed their index counterparts in the twelve months through June 2025 — a period marked by tariff disputes, elections and geopolitical swings. “Conventional wisdom says active managers should better manage those complexities,” Armour said, “but performance says otherwise.”
If human managers struggle to beat the index, the question becomes whether removing humans entirely solves the problem or compounds it.
There is one argument in Finq’s favor that the data supports convincingly. Dalbar’s 2025 Quantitative Analysis of Investor Behavior report found that the average equity fund investor earned 8.5 percentage points less than the S&P 500 in 2024. The culprit, according to Dalbar, wasn’t poor stock selection — it was psychology. Loss aversion, herd behavior and panic selling consistently erode returns.
An AI doesn’t panic. It doesn’t chase headlines or sell at the bottom. That behavioral advantage is real, even if it hasn’t yet translated into consistent outperformance.
The CFA Institute’s 2025 publication AI in Asset Management: Tools, Applications, and Frontiers frames the current moment carefully: AI should “supplement professional judgment,” not replace it. A companion piece in the Financial Analysts Journal described portfolio managers evolving from decision-makers into “stewards of machine-driven models” — a role that sounds closer to oversight than obsolescence.
Finq’s ETFs carry the risks you’d expect from a new, untested strategy. The prospectus flags high portfolio turnover, model and data risk, concentration in a limited number of holdings and — for AINT specifically — the theoretically unlimited losses that come with short selling. There is no performance history to evaluate. These funds are, for now, a thesis in search of a track record.
The broader question is whether fully autonomous AI-managed investing represents a genuine structural shift or simply the latest iteration of a promise the industry has been making, and failing to deliver on, for nearly a decade. The answer, as always in investing, will come from returns. And for now, the clock is just starting.

articles.title: How Liberty Mutual Insurance Is Using Data And AI To Deliver Value To Its Customers And Employees
articles.query: site:forbes.com ("generative AI" OR ChatGPT OR LLM) (finance OR bank OR investment OR insurance OR trading)
articles.text:
Liberty Mutual's Global CIO, Monica Caldas, details the company's strategic integration of data and AI, including generative AI, to enhance customer and employee value. This approach unifies their technology ecosystem, driving innovation and competitive advantage. Liberty Mutual's AI journey began with predictive analytics, evolving into rapid GenAI adoption through platforms like LibertyGPT, now used by 74% of employees. The company fosters an AI-driven culture via extensive upskilling, training, and a "Digital Progression Framework" to embed AI into daily workflows. Measurable results include improved operational efficiency, significant time savings, and enhanced experiences. A robust Responsible AI Steering Committee ensures ethical, compliant, and transparent AI deployment, balancing innovation with accountability for future growth.
How are data and AI being used to deliver value to customers and employees in the insurance industry? This is among the questions that I recently posed to Monica Caldas, Global Chief Information Officer (CIO) of Liberty Mutual Insurance. Founded in Boston, Massachusetts in 1912, Liberty Mutual today is the sixth largest property and casualty insurance company in the world and ranks 87 th on the Fortune 100 list of largest U.S. corporations.
Caldas, who has served in a CIO capacity at Liberty Mutual since 2018 previously held CIO roles at General Electric (GE). Today, as Global CIO at Liberty Mutual, Caldas leads a global technology organization of more than 5,500 employees across 27 countries. Caldas explains, “Our mission is to unify our technology ecosystem into one cohesive, high-performing enterprise. This structure enables us to accelerate innovation, strengthen our competitive advantage, and deliver consistent value across markets.” Core to this mission are data and AI.
At Liberty Mutual, technology is designed to operate as a unified enterprise engine—owning IT operations, engineering, AI and GenAI capabilities, and the data ecosystem that enables intelligent decision-making at scale. This model reflects a deliberate choice: to embed data and intelligence directly into the fabric of how the company operates, rather than treating them as standalone functions.
From this foundation, Caldas—alongside the Chief Operating Officer co-leads the company’s global enterprise data and data science office, sponsoring initiatives spanning the establishment of data fundamentals of domain, quality and data products across the company and innovative ways to accelerate value. Caldas comments, “We are balancing global integration with local delivery and embedding a focus on reusability, velocity, quality, and resiliency. This approach has positioned Liberty Mutual for its next phase of strategic growth.”
“At Liberty Mutual, embracing data and AI isn’t a technology initiative, it’s a core part of how we run the business,” explains Caldas. “The conversations I have with my peers at the executive leadership table are centered on how data and AI enable better decisions, smarter operations, and more meaningful experiences for our customers and employees.”
Caldas notes that Liberty Mutual’s AI journey began well before the rise of generative AI. “Our early efforts focused on predictive capabilities that strengthened core processes, such as underwriting completeness and claims forecasting, helping us plan capacity and manage risk more effectively,” she says. “Those investments gave us the discipline and foundation to adopt GenAI thoughtfully when it emerged.”
“As an insurance company, we didn’t start at step one in terms of data and artificial intelligence capabilities.” Caldas notes, “We’ve been leveraging data, data science, and machine learning for many years to help us understand how we can better serve our customers.” She notes, “When GenAI emerged in 2022, we quickly recognized its transformative potential not just in terms of operational efficiency, but how we serve our customers and empower our employees.”
Liberty Mutual is taking a hands-on approach to data and AI adoption across the firm. This begins with developing a shared vocabulary and understanding of what technology can do to improve business outcomes, says Caldas. Corporate learning initiatives include:
Caldas comments, “These efforts have already delivered measurable results—improving efficiency, reducing costs, and enhancing customer experience.”
Building a Data and AI driven business culture remains an ongoing challenge for many organizations. According to a just published survey of Fortune 1000 data and AI executives, 93% of respondents report that people and cultural challenges represent the greatest impediment to data and AI adoption within their firms.
“Our leadership believes that technology transformation is about people as much as systems,” notes Caldas. She continues, “We’ve invested heavily in upskilling our workforce, ensuring employees have the right tools, training, and guidance for responsible AI use, continuous learning and skill development. That commitment is helping us build a future-ready, resilient organization.”
Caldas adds that generative AI represents a fundamentally new way of working. “This shift applies to everyone, whether you're an engineer, a Claims professional or a lawyer. Our goal has been to make these capabilities approachable, helping people understand how AI can meaningfully support their work and decision making.” She notes, “Integrating AI into the lives of 40,000 employees has been intentional, with a strong emphasis on hands-on experience and practical application.”
To support this approach, Liberty Mutual has established a Digital Progression Framework that enables employees to learn, experiment, and innovate responsibly. Caldas explains, “Through Everyday AI , we encourage teams to explore practical ways generative AI can simplify their day-to-day work, from drafting communications to analyzing data.” She continues, “These efforts are supported by a growing learning ecosystem, including a GenAI Hub for hands-on guidance, an AI@Liberty Community for peer collaboration, a Responsible AI Steering Committee and a Change Champion Network that helps teams adopt and integrate new tools.”
“Our goal is to embed AI into the core way of working. We’re not just improving speed and quality--we’re giving people the confidence and capacity to focus on what matters most: solving real problems and delivering meaningful outcomes for our customers.”. She continues, “Ultimately, we’re inviting employees in, empowering them to see that AI is a fundamental enabler for everything they can do, empowering them to imagine what’s possible, and enabling them to apply AI in thoughtful, innovative ways every day.”
Ultimately, the success of Liberty Mutual’s data and AI investments will be defined not by the number of tools deployed, but by the measurable business outcomes they enable. Caldas explains, “With strong sponsorship from the executive leadership team, we’re embedding AI directly into core business processes such as underwriting, claims, and customer service,” explains Caldas. Championed by the executive leadership team, we’re embedding AI into core processes like underwriting, claims, and customer service.” For example, AI-powered capabilities are helping Liberty Mutual underwriters make faster, more informed decisions, while generative AI copilots assist claims teams through tasks such as document summarization and workflow automation—reducing friction and freeing up capacity for higher-value work.
Caldas notes that Liberty Mutual evaluates the value of its data and AI investments across three key dimensions: operational efficiency, impact, and adoption. She elaborates:
“Our transformational efforts are delivering tangible results,” says Caldas. She continues, “In our investments business unit we have modernized core systems, migrated data to the cloud, deployed GenAI as part of everyday work, and are now advancing our strategy toward agentic AI.” Caldas explains, “These outcomes point to a bold, disciplined and pragmatic approach not only to eliminate technical debt but also unlock capacity for innovation, positioning Liberty Mutual to deliver faster, more secure digital experiences and sustain long-term growth to support the company’s promise of being there for customers 24/7.”
Highlighting the critical importance of Responsible AI, Caldas explains, “We established a Responsible AI Steering Committee that brings together leaders from Technology, Legal, Privacy, Security, and HR to ensure that our use of AI is responsible, transparent, and aligned with our company values.”
Caldas notes, “This group Committee governs both risks and opportunities, balancing defensive and offensive, as well as pace and accountability.” She continues, “This group ensures that every AI innovation meets our standards for governance, ethics, and compliance—balancing the need for speed and experimentation with the responsibility to protect our customers and brand.”
“Responsible AI is about risk and compliance as well as how we empower our teams to experiment safely, align to evolving regulations, and create measurable business value,” notes Caldas. She continues, “We’ve been thoughtful about governance long before GenAI became mainstream. We had already built the scaffolding—data pipelines, model testing frameworks, and internal structures—that allowed us to adopt GenAI responsibly.”
Caldas concludes, “Governance is how you scale trust. It’s not just policies, its pace, visibility, accountability, applied consistently across the enterprise.”
Across Liberty Mutual, GenAI is creating the opportunity to reimagine how work gets done. Caldas explains, “At the heart of our philosophy is the notion that we want to unleash human potential.” Liberty Mutual plans to expand its use of GenAI across the business units in alignment with the business aspirations of the company, says Caldas.
“We have been disciplined in how we have moved forward with our 35 use cases which are now live and within the construct of our governance mechanisms,” says Caldas. “Within this, is the idea that we have to continue to operate with the best tools and capabilities so that our employees can deploy their creativity and domain expertise towards outcomes that matter most.” She elaborates, “This means enabling our employees to focus on deep work while streamlining more routine aspects to the workflows.”
Looking ahead, Caldas outlines a clear vision for the role of technology, noting, “Our vision is that technology is a force multiplier in support of our business aspirations.” She continues, “AI is another powerful capability in our toolbox—but one that represents a shift from deterministic systems to more dynamic, context-aware technologies. That shift gives our teams greater flexibility and adaptability to the context in near real time.” She adds, “We are unlocking the full value of our data, ensuring that real-time, AI-ready information can seamlessly integrate with large language models and autonomous agents.”
Caldas concludes, “We will continue to focus on developing a culture of adoption, training our employees for responsible use of GenAI, and alignment to our business goals in how we plan to develop products and services to best serve our customers.” She sums up, “As we embed new AI capabilities directly into workflows, we’re enabling automation and augmentation that accelerate decision-making and free our people to focus on higher-value work. We are unlocking human potential for a resilient and future ready enterprise.”

articles.title: Finny Raises $17 Million As It Seeks To Upend Advisor Prospecting With Artificial Intelligence
articles.query: site:forbes.com (fintech OR "wealth management" OR "asset management" OR payments) ("artificial intelligence" OR "machine learning")
articles.text:
In Finny’s first 18 months, cofounder and CEO Eden Ovadia, lived at the office. Not in the hyperbolic sense, Finny’s headquarters consisted of two conference rooms, one of which doubled as a bedroom each night. The spartan setup was intentional, meant to signal commitment to skeptical Silicon Valley investors who questioned the company’s decision to build in New York City rather than San Francisco. Ovadia, 27, and her cofounders, Stanford computer science grad Victoria Toli, 27, and machine learning researcher Theodore Janson, 27, were determined to prove they were all in on disrupting U.S. wealth management with an artificial intelligence driven sales and marketing tool that functions like a dating app for financial advisers and prospective clients. The three were featured in Forbes Under30 in 2026 on the AI list .
So far, investors appear convinced. In its recent Series A round, Finny raised $17 million in funding co-led by Venrock, former Vanguard chairman and CEO William McNabb, Activant and Altruist’s Jason Wenk and Y Combinator, among others. Founded in 2024 by three AI natives, Finny has raised more than $20 million in total, serves over 500 advisory firms, including Focus Financial Partners, Integrated Partners and Apollon Wealth Management, and is valued at roughly $150 million.
Convincing early backers was not automatic. Prior to investing, Y Combinator partner Michael Seibel questioned the very premise of the business. “I went in thinking, do people really need financial advisers, or can you just put money in Vanguard, follow a 60/40 rule and call it a day?” he said. “But they showed me how much more complex the financial life of the non-uber wealthy have become. Stock based compensation, multiple jobs, side businesses. All of it makes personalized advice far more valuable than I expected.”
The skepticism was understandable. Wealth management, which is dominated by older generation advisors and is notoriously resistant to disrupting tried and true methods. Ask any Forbes Top Advisor, it is a people business anchored by a system of referral driven relationships. Still, Venrock partner Nick Beim believes Finny’s software supports so-called “organic growth” in asset gathering. “This is the holy grail of the wealth management industry,” he says, “Finny is a shortcut to that Holy Grail.”
Finny breaks the process into three layers. First, its artificial intelligence aggregates publicly available information alongside licensed private data, building a database of over 300 million potential prospects in North America. Within that data set, the system continually flags “money motion events” such as career changes, inheritance, marriage, or liquidity events like cashing out after selling your company or taking it public. Second, the data is processed through Finny’s prioritization algorithm, which assigns each prospect with an “F-score” that functions like a dating app for advisors and clients – linking them based on their commonalities, expertise and niche fit. Finally, messaging is personalized based on these signals. Meanwhile in an effort to always “stay fresh”, Finny processes between six and ten billion data points daily which is fed into their algorithm.
Finny, which offers individual advisor subscriptions starting at $500 per month, is not alone in its efforts to capitalize on AI powered prospecting for financial advisors. It joins ZoomInfo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, SalesLoft, Crystal, Apollo, Smart Assets and Blackrock’s Aladdin. Virtually all of these platforms have baked AI into their software.
Thomas Manetta, former vice president at Charles Schwab and the founder of Manetta Wealth, said that while he only began using Finny seriously three months ago. “I’ve spent maybe twelve hours a month using Finny,” he said, “and from that I’ve already closed a five million dollar client.”
Despite some early successes, Finny faces an uphill battle convincing wealth managers to hand over their prospecting to AI. Forbes spoke to a half a dozen wealth advisors overseeing billions in assets under management, a consistent refrain emerged. Word of mouth, and trusted personal relationships, remains king.
Finny’s argument is not against referrals themselves, but against how they scale. Traditional referrals are constrained by adviser time, limiting how much organic growth even the most successful firms can generate. “Referrals scale linearly with your time, and time is your most valuable resource,” says Ovadia. “If it takes ten hours of dinners to generate one referral, we are building a system that can deliver that same outcome, but one that operates continuously, even when you are sleeping or on a golf course.”
Finny’s bet on exponential organic growth does not assume that clients will suddenly trust algorithms more than people, but rather, that systems can start replicating the outcomes of referral behavior without consuming the adviser’s personal time.
Industry research suggests the constraint is real. Cerulli reports that 83% of registered investment advisors cite time limitations and insufficient support as significant barriers to growth – a finding echoed by Fidelity . Which also reports that 42% of advisor firms rank marketing and business development growth as a top priority. Meanwhile, McKinsey & Company estimates the wealth management industry is on track to face a shortage of roughly 100,000 advisors by 2034, even as fee revenue has grown substantially from about $150 billion in 2015 to roughly $260 billion in 2024.
Will wealth managers become dinosaurs as artificial intelligence invades financial services, or will smart AI tools from firms like Finny help the best of them scale their businesses rapidly? Stay tuned.

articles.title: The Rise Of Algorithmic Trading: How AI Is Reshaping Financial Markets
articles.query: site:forbes.com "artificial intelligence" (trading OR "stock market" OR portfolio OR "hedge fund")
articles.text:
Algorithmic trading is no longer the exclusive domain of niche quantitative firms—it has become the backbone of modern financial markets. I am already seeing the significant impact AI-driven strategies are having on market dynamics. In 2024 alone, high-frequency trading algorithms generated $10.4 billion in revenue, and this figure is projected to soar to $16 billion by 2030. This isn’t just growth; it’s a redefinition of how markets function, driven by the relentless pace of innovation.
As someone who has witnessed this evolution firsthand through our work with leading financial institutions, I've seen how the convergence of artificial intelligence, agile infrastructure, and new regulatory demands is opening new opportunities for organizations ready to embrace change. It’s important to clarify, however, that algorithmic trading is a broad field—not every strategy hinges on ultra-low latency or high-frequency trading (HFT) speeds. While HFT certainly operates in the realm of microseconds and below, many algo trading operations leverage diverse timeframes and methods for trade placement, focusing more on intelligence than sheer speed.
The algorithmic trading market's expansion reflects the broader digitization of financial services. Beyond institutional high-frequency trading, retail algorithmic platforms now command over $11 billion in global spending, with retail usage growing at an impressive 10.8% annually. This growth stems from several key drivers: zero-commission brokerage models, expanded asset coverage (including cryptocurrency and fractional futures) and the democratization of trading tools through API-first brokers.
What makes this particularly interesting is the geographic distribution. While North America maintains approximately 32% of global high-frequency trading flow, Europe captures 28%, and Asia-Pacific secures 25%. This distributed landscape creates unique infrastructure challenges and opportunities for technology providers who can deliver consistent performance across multiple jurisdictions.
A common misconception is that algorithmic trading is synonymous with ultra-low latency. In reality, the true differentiator for most successful firms is their expertise in data science—specifically, the use of AI, machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) models to better understand market sentiment and perform risk modelling more effectively than competitors. These sophisticated models form intellectual property at the core of specialized algorithmic trading firms.
This reliance on proprietary ML/DL models has redefined the infrastructure landscape. The race is less about brute force or raw clock speeds, and more about building secure, high-performance environments that prioritize IP protection. Algo trading customers are some of the most technically advanced and protective of their intellectual property, often disclosing only technical requirements to vendors and fiercely safeguarding the details of their trading models.
While HFT still pushes the limits of sub-microsecond execution—with some firms using FPGA-accelerated systems for tick-to-trade times below 100 nanoseconds—most organizations are focused on achieving the most predictive, robust AI models. The technology stack extends beyond compute to security, compliance, and operational resilience. For instance, one leading European trading organization recently invested over €1 billion in Nordic data centers—not just to chase speed, but to support AI-driven forecasts across 50,000+ financial instruments, and to build scalable solutions capable of handling exponential data growth.
It's here that forward-thinking infrastructure plays a crucial role. For algorithmic trading firms, achieving competitive advantage is rooted in integrated compute and storage built around their IP, coupled with operational resilience and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) objectives. As sustainability becomes a strategic priority, modern data centers—optimized for efficiency and backed by reliable partners—are helping firms build greener, more responsible trading operations.
This advancing frontier can leave traditional institutions struggling to keep pace. Most players in capital markets, investment banking, and wealth management built their proprietary tools and algorithms years ago. Now, many are exploring ways to enhance their existing intellectual property with AI acceleration or unconventional methods like CPU overclocking. As technology evolves rapidly, these firms are striving to stay ahead of the competition by modernizing their strategies and tools.
Understanding the evolving needs of technology providers in ultra-low-latency environments is critical. At Dell Technologies, we’re focused on delivering integrated, resilient, and sustainable infrastructures that enable clients to unlock the full potential of AI and ML. By prioritizing innovation and adaptability, we aim to support the most demanding performance requirements while driving competitive value for algorithmic trading and beyond. Our solutions are designed to empower businesses with the tools they need to stay ahead in this fast-paced, technology-driven landscape.
Working with top trading firms reveals several critical insights about the modern algorithmic trading environment. As firms move to remote and distributed data centers, the logistical complexities grow. At the same time, firms demand infrastructure that supports advanced AI workloads yet keeps operations seamless and secure. The key is to deliver solutions—like advanced liquid cooling, high-performance networking, and white-glove deployment—that enable the analysis of trillions of data points per day while maintaining operational redundancy and trust in the underlying systems.
Regulatory requirements add another layer of complexity. The European Union's RTS 6 revision enforces 50-microsecond gateway timestamping and per-instrument order-to-trade ratio caps. Meanwhile, Australia's ASIC CP 361 rewrite imposes microsecond timestamps with new reporting requirements. This regulatory fragmentation creates compliance costs estimated at £8-12 million per tier-1 cross-listed dealer.
Financial institutions must navigate these requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The organizations that succeed are those implementing unified control layers that can handle regulatory compliance within the critical path without introducing latency penalties.
The future of algorithmic trading will likely be defined by several key trends. Quantum-AI risk engines represent a $2.86 billion sub-market projected to reach $24 billion by 2033, focusing on systemic shock modeling and quantum-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations. Explainable AI requirements are becoming mandatory as regulators demand transparency in algorithmic decision-making.
Perhaps most significantly, the industry is experiencing a shift in monetization models. While spread capture remains important, leading firms are expanding into execution-as-a-service offerings and alternative data resale. This diversification requires infrastructure that can support both ultra-low latency trading and data-intensive analytics workloads.
Algorithmic trading firms face escalating technological demands, complex regulatory landscapes, and fierce competition. Success hinges on more than just powerful infrastructure—it requires integrated solutions capable of handling everything from microsecond trading to massive AI-driven data analysis.
Cutting-edge technologies like Dell PowerEdge with NVIDIA RTX Pro Blackwell Server Edition GPUs , are transforming the industry by enabling firms to tackle advanced workloads such as explainable AI. These high-performance solutions provide the computational power and scalability needed to turn technological complexity into a competitive advantage while advancing sustainability and trust in financial markets.
Ready to explore how advanced infrastructure solutions can transform your algorithmic trading capabilities? Connect with your Dell Technologies account executive or visit our financial solutions page to discover how we’re helping leading firms navigate the future of financial markets.

articles.title: Crypto Traders Trust These AI Agents The Most
articles.query: site:forbes.com ("algorithmic trading" OR "AI trading" OR "quantitative trading" OR "robo-advisor")
articles.text:
Imagine handing over your investment portfolio to a robot that never sleeps, constantly monitors dozens of markets, and rebalances your holdings every few minutes to chase the best returns. It sounds like science fiction, but in the crypto world, it’s increasingly reality. AI trading agents (autonomous software programs that execute financial strategies on behalf of users) have exploded in 2025 , managing tens of millions of dollars and promising yields that make traditional savings accounts look quaint.
Yet here's the paradox: in an industry built on the mantra "don't trust, verify," why would anyone trust an AI to manage their money?
The skepticism is well-founded. AI models often operate as "black boxes," making decisions users can't always parse. Data feeds can be manipulated, sending agents chasing phantom opportunities. And psychologically, there's the discomfort of ceding control – even if the math says the robot is smarter, many traders simply prefer to keep their hands on the wheel.
Despite these hurdles, a handful of AI agents have managed to gain popularity and earn the crypto community's trust through a combination of transparent operations, proven track records, and – crucially – cold, hard returns.
The appeal of AI agents in crypto isn’t hard to understand once you grasp the underlying opportunity. Decentralized finance, or DeFi, has created a parallel financial system where anyone with an internet connection can lend, borrow, trade, and earn yields without traditional banks or brokers. But DeFi is also fragmented and fast-moving. Interest rates on stablecoin lending might be 8% on one protocol, 12% on another, and 15% on a third, for example, and those rates can shift by the hour as capital flows in and out.
A savvy trader who manually monitors these opportunities and moves funds accordingly can significantly outperform someone who parks money in a single place. The problem? That requires constant attention, technical knowledge, and the willingness to pay gas fees (transaction costs) every time you rebalance.
This is where AI agents become genuinely useful rather than merely novel. They can monitor dozens of protocols simultaneously, execute rebalancing strategies in milliseconds, and operate 24/7 without fatigue or emotion.
Giza’s Autonomous Revenue Management Agent has become a popular tool to optimize stablecoin yields – digital dollars that are supposed to hold their value – ARMA automatically shifts user funds between lending protocols like Aave and Compound to capture the best interest rates.
Giza has announced that ARMA has crossed $20 million in 'assets under agent,’ positioning it among the leading AI agent protocols. ARMA is described as a flagship stablecoin yield agent operating via non-custodial smart accounts with session keys that restrict its permissions, ensuring users retain custody of their assets. According to Giza’s own numbers, by July 2025 ARMA had achieved over $10 million AUA and processed more than $400 million in cumulative volume. Giza also claims that its agents deliver +83% higher yields over static positions through continuous optimization.
While ARMA focuses on stablecoins, ZyFAI casts a wider net. This platform lets users launch customized vaults (automated investment pools) that hunt for high yields across multiple blockchain networks. With about $7.5 million in total value locked, the crypto industry’s metric for assets under management, ZyFAI operates on Base, Arbitrum, Sonic, and Plasma networks.
What sets ZyFAI apart is its "set-and-forget" appeal. The agent uses real-time data to move funds into high-yield opportunities and automatically compounds returns, all while the user does nothing. For traders seeking passive income across multiple chains, ZyFAI has become a trusted aggregator that does the heavy lifting.
Sometimes trust comes from association. Mamo, built by the team behind the Moonwell protocol and integrated into Coinbase's Base network, benefits from the credibility of established crypto institutions. Launched in August 2025, Mamo has already received the thumbs up from Brian Armstrong , CEO of Coinbase (one of the agent’s backers) as well as numerous other traders.
What makes Mamo effective is its simplicity. It runs inside a chat-style interface on the Base wallet app, making it accessible to users who might find traditional DeFi, where users trade without intermediaries, intimidating. With about 3,700 active users and over $90 million rebalanced to date, Mamo has proven that a (relatively) user-friendly experience, combined with institutional backing and non-custodial architecture, can rapidly build trust even among crypto newcomers.
Not all AI agents focus on passive yield. Bankr operates as a "DeFi autopilot" for active traders, executing complex commands through natural language. Want to set a limit order for a memecoin for after midnight? Bridge assets from Ethereum to Polygon? Bankr handles it across multiple chains (Base, Ethereum, Polygon, and Solana) without users needing to navigate multiple decentralized apps.
Backed by Coinbase Ventures, Bankr doesn't hold user funds or accumulate TVL. Instead, it earns trust through utility: thousands of traders use it weekly to execute strategies that would otherwise require technical expertise and constant attention. For degens (crypto slang for risk-taking traders), Bankr has become an indispensable co-pilot.
What unites these trusted agents is a formula: transparency plus performance plus security. They've addressed the crypto community's trust concerns not through marketing, but through verifiable track records, non-custodial designs, security audits, and consistent returns.
The sector’s growth speaks volumes. From essentially zero only a few years ago, AI agents now manage over $100 million across the ecosystem. Yet, this is minuscule in comparison to both the Web2 (non-crypto) equivalent and future Web3 automation potential. Crypto users have serious trust issues due to the industries’ numerous past fiascos which leads to slow adoption until trust is established. Trust can and should come from cryptographic solutions. The three main questions that users should ask themselves are:
An unclear answer to any of these questions will stop many users from ever depositing money. One project that has managed to provide good answers is the treasury management agent Talos, incubated by Arbitrum. The agent manages a portfolio and autonomously rebalances across multiple tokenized vaults. Talos is running in a TEE cloud that is relatively verifiable and decentralized. The agent is powered by a decentralized key management system where the private key has never left a secure enclave. Plus, a transparent upgrade path is ensured by public multi-sig governance for each new upgrade proposal. That’s an example of what a thorough answer to the above-mentioned questions might look like when you’re evaluating AI tools for crypto trading.
For crypto traders, the age of AI-managed portfolios is already here. The agents that have earned the community's trust aren't perfect, but they're proving that with the right combination of transparency, security, and results, even an industry built on "don't trust, verify" can learn to trust the machines.

articles.title: AI-Powered Financial Planning And The Rise Of Personalized Financial Independence Tools
articles.query: site:forbes.com ("algorithmic trading" OR "AI trading" OR "quantitative trading" OR "robo-advisor")
articles.text:
The personal financial planning industry is undergoing its most significant transformation since the advent of online banking. Only 35% of Americans have a financial plan, with high costs, limited access to advisors and discomfort discussing finances serving as primary barriers. Now, artificial intelligence is changing that equation, offering deep personalized insights without the referral fees and conflicts of interest that have long plagued traditional advisory services.
The market is responding. The AI-Powered Personal Finance Management Market was valued at $1.37 billion in 2024 and is expected to reach $2.36 billion by 2032, growing at a 7% compound annual growth rate. More telling, 57% of finance professionals are already using AI in their operations, with another 14% planning implementation.
Traditional financial planning has always carried an inherent tension. Advisors charging 1-2% of assets under management had built-in incentives to recommend certain products, and fee structures kept sophisticated planning tools accessible only to high-net-worth individuals. AI-powered platforms are disrupting this model by offering objective scenario analysis, deep financial projections, and personalized planning at a fraction of the cost—or sometimes free.
AI-powered tools can analyze a household's full financial picture—from income and assets to goals and risks—to generate personalized strategies that adjust to life changes like delayed retirement, unexpected healthcare costs or new passions in later years.
Take Hiro, founded by Ethan Bloch , the entrepreneur behind the successful fintech company Digit. After stepping down from Digit in 2023, Bloch was inspired by OpenAI’s advances to build "the thing I had been wanting to do with Digit for the last 10 years". Hiro takes a conversational approach to financial planning, walking users through plan creation via chat and enabling what-if scenarios like "Buy a house for 1 million or 1.5 million? Take a year off work?" The platform tracks income and spending across all accounts, allows users to link accounts, upload CSVs, drop in PDFs, or manually edit balances, and uses purpose-built tools to excel at financial math with verifiable calculations.
The AI-powered financial planning market has evolved into four distinct quadrants based on two critical dimensions: sophistication level (basic budgeting vs. comprehensive planning) and target market (consumer direct-to-consumer vs. advisor-focused B2B tools).
These platforms offer comprehensive financial planning directly to consumers, bypassing traditional advisors entirely. They provide scenario modeling, tax optimization, retirement projections, and net worth tracking—capabilities once reserved for wealthy clients with dedicated CFPs.
Wealthfront , Wealthfront, managing over $41 billion in discretionary client assets (and more than $88 billion in total client assets including cash accounts), represents the mature end of this quadrant. The platform charges a 0.25% annual advisory fee with a $500 minimum, provides automated tax-loss harvesting for all taxable accounts, and offers direct indexing options at multiple levels — including S&P 500 Direct (0.09% fee, $5,000 minimum) and Nasdaq-100 Direct (0.12% fee, $5,000 minimum), as well as full-scale direct indexing for accounts over $100,000. Wealthfront reports a three-year annualized return of 17.97%, significantly outperforming peer benchmarks cited in external analyses.
Betterment , the largest independent robo-advisor with $65 billion in AUM serving approximately 900,000 clients, takes a different approach. Betterment earned top honors as the best robo-advisor overall in Bankrate's 2025 reviews . The platform charges a 0.25% annual fee for its Digital Plan with no minimum balance requirement, while its Premium Plan costs 0.65% annually and requires a $100,000 minimum but includes unlimited access to certified financial planners.
The newer entrants like Hiro and Tendi are pushing boundaries further by eliminating advisory fees entirely and focusing on conversational AI interfaces that make sophisticated planning accessible to average consumers.
Market Position: These platforms are growing rapidly among younger demographics and middle-income households who were previously underserved. Research indicates nearly half of American consumers are either currently using or seriously considering AI-driven financial management solutions, with younger demographics leading this adoption trend.
These platforms don't replace financial advisors—they supercharge them. By automating analysis and generating insights from complex documents like tax returns, estate plans, and insurance policies, they enable advisors to serve more clients with deeper, more comprehensive planning.
eMoney Advisor , owned by Fidelity, maintains 28.20% market share as the current market leader, though down slightly from 29.55% in 2024. The platform emphasizes cash-flow planning and the ability to model plans for estate, retirement and education-funding purposes, with pricing starting at $2,400-$3,600 per advisor annually. The platform manages over $1 trillion in client assets for advisors from firms like TD Ameritrade and New York Life.
RightCapital is rapidly gaining ground. The platform captured 20.68% market share and shows a strong growth trajectory by offering advisors powerful features at mid-market pricing. RightCapital handles most daily planning needs without compromising speed, allowing advisors to toggle between goal and cash-flow views in the same plan with year-by-year tax projections alongside lifetime probability graphs.
FP Alpha takes a different approach by focusing specifically on document analysis. The platform reads clients' tax returns, wills, trusts, and insurance policies, instantly summarizing key data, identifying actionable planning insights, quantifying the value of advice, and driving more revenue to the advisor. As Joel Bruckenstein, founder of the Technology Tools for Today (T3) Conference, notes in a testimonial: "FP Alpha provides advisors with a competitive advantage as fee-compression continues to affect the advisory space. The technology provides impactful recommendations with limited insight into a prospect's financial and personal circumstances".
Market Position: These tools are becoming essential infrastructure. AI adoption in finance surged from 45% in 2022 to an expected 85% by 2025 , with 60% of companies using AI across multiple business areas. Advisors who don't adopt these platforms risk being left behind by competitors who can serve clients faster and more comprehensively.
These platforms focus on budgeting, expense tracking, and basic financial management. While less sophisticated than full planning platforms, they serve an important role as entry points for financial literacy.
Cleo is a chatbot-driven personal finance assistant utilizing AI with an engaging and intuitive approach to budgeting, analyzing financial data to offer personalized advice and helping users stay on top of spending. Monarch Money provides customized budgeting plans that adapt to individual user needs and goals, tracking income and expenses while visualizing financial progress over time.
Market Position: These platforms capture users early in their financial journey and often serve as feeders to more sophisticated tools as users' wealth and complexity grow.
These tools solve specific pain points in advisor workflows—meeting notes, tax return analysis, presentation creation—without attempting comprehensive planning.
Jump AI is a meeting note-taking tool purpose-built for financial advisors to address the major pain point of post-meeting documentation and follow-up, saving teams at least 30 minutes per meeting. Holistiplan enables advisors to summarize and organize data in tax returns for analysis, scenario comparison, and advice delivery.
Market Position: These specialized tools are increasingly becoming table stakes for advisory practices focused on operational efficiency.
Traditional financial planning software leaders like eMoney and MoneyGuidePro are fighting to maintain relevance. MoneyGuidePro's market share dropped from 33% in 2024 to 22.79% in 2025, suggesting the established players are under pressure. Development at MoneyGuidePro has slowed since the Envestnet acquisition, and survey data show advanced users migrating to newer platforms.
These incumbents have deep integration with broker-dealers and major financial institutions, but they risk being disrupted by more agile competitors with native AI capabilities. MoneyGuidePro is a goals-based application ideal for advisors servicing clients in accumulation stages or with less than $1 million of investable assets, priced between $1,300 and $2,000.
Platforms like Wealthfront and Betterment, which started as simple automated portfolio management tools, are evolving into comprehensive financial planning platforms. They're moving upstream, adding features like estate planning, tax optimization, and human advisor access that were once the exclusive domain of traditional wealth management.
Wealthfront offers smart financial advice via the Path tool, providing projections and recommendations, along with daily rebalancing to maintain target allocation. Meanwhile, Betterment has introduced cryptocurrency portfolios and socially responsible investing options, signaling adaptability to modern preferences.
Companies like Hiro, Tendi, and Parthean are being built from the ground up with AI as their core technology, not bolted on as a feature. This architectural advantage allows them to offer capabilities—like natural language financial planning or instant document analysis—that legacy platforms struggle to match.
The current generation of AI-powered financial planning tools offers capabilities that weren't possible even two years ago:
Natural Language Processing for Accessibility Advancements in natural language processing and conversational AI improve the accessibility of financial advice, with advisors using NLP tools to draft personalized client communications and create detailed financial reports.
Scenario Modeling at Scale With AI, FP&A teams can quickly model multiple "what-if" scenarios to evaluate the potential outcomes of different strategies, supporting smarter, data-driven decision-making in uncertain or dynamic conditions.
Document Intelligence AI-driven technology "reads" clients' tax returns, wills, trusts, and insurance policies, instantly summarizing key data and identifying actionable planning insights.
Predictive Analytics AI can leverage predictive analytics to analyze historical and current data, providing insights that help anticipate future trends and outcomes with greater accuracy.
Democratization Will Accelerate AI-driven financial advice is creating a more equitable financial landscape where everyone—not just the wealthy—can plan confidently for the future. The cost differential is dramatic: Robo-advisor fees typically range from zero to 0.35% of assets under management, compared to traditional advisor fees of 1-2%.
Human + AI Hybrid Models Will Dominate Checking AI-generated advice with a professional is important, with advisors moving beyond static annual reviews to offer real-time, adaptive guidance that changes with life circumstances. The winning model won't be AI replacing humans, but AI augmenting human advisors to serve more clients better.
Consolidation Among Incumbents The market has too many players offering similar capabilities. Expect M&A activity as established platforms acquire AI capabilities and upstarts seek distribution. Betterment's February 2025 acquisition of Ellevest signals this trend.
Enterprise Integration The global financial planning software market is projected to reach $18.2 billion by 2033 , growing at a robust 15.5% CAGR. Much of this growth will come from enterprise adoption as banks, broker-dealers, and large RIAs standardize on comprehensive platforms.
AI-powered financial planning represents a genuine democratization of sophisticated financial services. For the first time, average consumers can access objective, comprehensive financial planning without paying exorbitant fees or navigating conflicted advice.
The technology is proven—specialized AI platforms like Tendi score significantly higher than general AI models on the Certified Financial Planner exam, demonstrating they can match or exceed human expertise in core planning concepts. The adoption curve is steep, with 57% of finance professionals already using AI and consumer adoption following rapidly.
For consumers, the calculus is straightforward: Platforms like Hero offer sophisticated scenario analysis, objective advice free of referral fees, and the ability to model everything from career changes to home purchases to early retirement—all at a fraction of traditional advisory costs.
For financial advisors, the message is equally clear: Advisory firms using advanced financial planning software experience 40% higher productivity , 35% improved client satisfaction, and 25% faster revenue growth. The technology isn't replacing advisors—it's making the best advisors better while eliminating the mediocre middle.
The AI-powered financial planning revolution is here. The only question is whether traditional players can adapt fast enough to compete.

articles.title: 3 Best Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks To Buy In 2026
articles.query: site:forbes.com "artificial intelligence" (trading OR "stock market" OR portfolio OR "hedge fund")
articles.text:
Wall Street analysts are concerned about an AI bubble despite growing infrastructure investments, which will continue in 2026 but not as fast. Nvidia, Microsoft and Alphabet are projected to remain the top AI stocks in 2026 based on their market dominance in AI chips and cloud services. The three tech giants are highly profitable and have strong growth potential despite market uncertainties.
The three best AI stocks in 2026 are likely to be familiar names — Nvidia, Microsoft and Alphabet.
Nvidia, which had a market capitalization more than $5 trillion in October, has been a driving force behind the artificial intelligence boom thanks to its dominance in AI chip design. Microsoft and Google have capitalized on the demand for generative AI by providing the cloud-services platforms to train and operate applications such as chatbots. With hundreds of billions of dollars being spent on AI, these companies are likely to be among the leading beneficiaries in 2026.
Read on to learn the criteria used to pick these stocks, how they passed the tests and what analysts are saying about the future of AI.
Wall Street has been abuzz about an AI bubble and the chances it will burst, washing away billions of dollars in value. The evidence of such a bubble is well-known:
Will the AI bubble burst in 2026? In October, I wrote about three scenarios: GenAI keeps booming, there’s a soft-landing in which valuations decline somewhat, and the OpenAI bankruptcy scenario, which brings it all down abruptly should the company be unable to raise more capital to fund its money-losing operations.
Since then, OpenAI may have opened up a path to an initial public offering. In 2026 or 2027, the maker of ChatGPT could go public, selling $60 billion in stock while keeping most shares private. Such an IPO would value the company at more than $1 trillion, according to an exclusive report by Reuters . Were this IPO to happen, the OpenAI bankruptcy scenario would become less likely.
I chose these stocks based on three criteria: strong growth forecasts, potential to exceed expectations, and high profitability. By applying these criteria to select these companies, chances increase their stock prices will rise – untarnished by the risk of bankruptcy that might frighten investors who buy stock in faster-growing, unprofitable companies.
Nvidia leads in revenue growth, profitability, and stock price appreciation. Microsoft and Alphabet are both growing and highly profitable and have enjoyed stock price appreciation – however, the numbers for these two are less impressive. Overall, Nvidia is riskier because investors have such high expectations for the company.
Nvidia controls about 90% of the market for graphics processing units used to train and operate AI chatbots and other generative AI applications. The company also provides systems on chips and application programming interfaces for data science, high-performance computing, and mobile and automotive applications.
Nvidia is expected to maintain its leadership position as the primary provider of GPUs – which became clear to me in May 2023, when the company issued a growth forecast signaling the rise of generative AI. That inspired me to write the book Brain Rush . As capital continues to flow into building global AI infrastructure, here's why this stock is a top choice:
Microsoft develops and licenses software, services and devices including the Windows operating system, Microsoft 365 (Office suite), the Azure cloud platform, the Xbox gaming system, and hardware such as Surface devices. The company says its strategy is based on cloud-first innovation and artificial intelligence.
Microsoft is leveraging its enterprise software dominance and position as the second-largest cloud provider to integrate and monetize AI across its entire ecosystem.
Alphabet is a leader in search advertising, cloud services and self-driving vehicles. GOOG is the world's third-largest technology company by revenue, after Amazon and Apple; the largest technology company by profit; and one of the world's most valuable companies.
The company has successfully navigated the shift to generative AI by integrating the technology into its core search product and building strong momentum in Google Cloud.
Analysts anticipate capital investment in cloud computing in 2026 will taper off, with significant variations among the largest companies. "After three years of unprecedented growth, U.S. hyperscalers are increasingly focused on investment returns and the impact of rising depreciation expenses on profitability," Dell'Oro Group analyst Baron Fung said, according to Investor’s Business Daily .
Leading Wall Street banks put numbers on their slowdown forecasts. Goldman Sachs sees cloud capital spending growing only 26% in 2026, not 54% like the year before. Morgan Stanley is more pessimistic, estimating a 2026 growth rate of 16%, which is significantly less than 56% in 2025. Evercore ISI expects a slowdown to 18% growth in 2026 from 64% in 2025, while Dell'Oro estimates 21% growth next year, “down from well over 50% in 2025,” wrote IBD .
Capital spending at both Amazon and Google is expected to grow about 11% in 2026. Meta's cloud spending will grow a still robust 42%, while Microsoft will increase outlays 22% and Oracle up 21%, IBD noted.
Companies' inability to generate enough revenue to offset their rapid investment has executives proceeding more cautiously. Hyperscalers’ data centers must generate 10 times current revenues “just to cover the annual depreciation costs of AI infrastructure,” Praetorian Capital said in a blog post featured by IBD .
Despite the mixed view of the future, Nvidia has a positive long-term view."We see $3 trillion to $4 trillion in AI infrastructure spend by the end of the decade," Nvidia Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress said on the company's second-quarter earnings call with analysts .
"We expect annual AI infrastructure investments to continue growing, driven by several factors — reasoning agentic AI requiring orders of magnitude more training and inference compute, global buildouts for sovereign AI, enterprise AI adoption, and the arrival of physical AI and robotics," Kress said.
As an AI bubble expands, analysts envision a possible slowdown coming. The nature and timing of that slowdown is difficult to predict. Before the boom slows, however, rapidly-growing, highly profitable providers of cloud services and AI chip designs may enjoy gains in their stock prices in 2026. Nvidia, Microsoft and Alphabet appear to be in the best position.

articles.title: The Surge Of AI In Crypto Trading: How AI Reshapes The Markets
articles.query: site:forbes.com "artificial intelligence" (trading OR "stock market" OR portfolio OR "hedge fund")
articles.text:
The world of cryptocurrency trading has always been synonymous with volatility. Traders constantly navigate price swings, regulatory uncertainty, and shifts in market sentiment. Yet, amidst this chaos, a transformative force is emerging: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML).
Liquidity Finders reports that by 2025, AI is projected to handle nearly 89% of global trading volume, revolutionizing markets from equities to decentralized crypto, highlighting its transformative impact on trading efficiency and accuracy.
These advanced technologies are now playing a central role in reshaping how we approach crypto trading, from predictive models and automated strategies to enhanced risk management. AI is quickly becoming the backbone of a more efficient and profitable future for crypto traders.
In the early days of cryptocurrency, trading was driven mainly by manual analysis. Human traders would monitor price charts, news cycles, and social media to make decisions. While this worked in simpler times, the rapid growth of the crypto market and the increasing number of available tokens made this approach impractical.
As the cryptocurrency landscape grew more complex, the need for faster, data-driven insights became clear. AI and ML models, which can process vast amounts of data in real time, were introduced to help traders make more informed decisions. These technologies analyze price movements, social sentiment, and even macroeconomic indicators to identify trends, predict price changes, and optimize trading strategies.
AI's evolution from a buzzword to a core component of crypto trading strategies signifies a new era for traders and investors alike. The introduction of machine learning systems that continuously adapt based on data patterns is revolutionizing how market predictions are made.
When it comes to trading, one of the most essential aspects is prediction. The ability to foresee price changes can give traders a significant edge, especially in a volatile market like cryptocurrency. A study analyzing AI-driven strategies for Bitcoin trading from 2018 to 2024 showed that an AI-led model achieved a total return of 1640%. This outperformance of conventional machine learning and buy-and-hold approaches underscores AI’s predictive power.
Historically, this has been challenging due to the market’s unpredictable nature. However, AI and ML are changing the world by delivering highly accurate predictions from complex datasets.
Machine learning models can process historical market data, trading volumes, and even real-time data, such as news and social media trends, to predict future market movements. These models use advanced algorithms, such as neural networks, that learn and improve over time. For instance, predictive models can suggest when to buy, hold, or sell based on real-time data analysis.
A notable example of AI's effectiveness comes from Numerai , a hedge fund that leverages machine learning to predict market trends. By pooling data from thousands of data scientists, Numerai creates models that outperform traditional ones. The success of this platform is a direct result of AI’s ability to enhance prediction accuracy, making it easier for investors to anticipate market movements.
This ability to predict price changes with high accuracy makes AI an invaluable tool for crypto traders, especially in an environment where volatility is the norm.
Gone are the days when traders had to spend countless hours manually executing trades based on market observations. In 2025, the market capitalization of AI crypto agents surged 29% to over $31 billion in just weeks, reflecting rapid adoption and investor confidence. GPT-5-powered AI trading bots demonstrated 15-25% outperformance over manual traders during volatile periods, with cases showing 25% returns in just one month on modest investments. Today, AI-driven trading bots have taken over, streamlining and automating the entire trading process.
AI-powered trading bots allow traders to set specific conditions, such as buying a crypto asset when its price drops below a certain level, and let the bot execute trades automatically when those conditions are met. This system eliminates human error and emotional decision-making, enabling trades to be executed instantly and efficiently. According to Tickeron , AI trading robots achieved remarkable annualized returns in 2025: 85% for ETH.X, 56% for OM.X, and 49% for XRP.X, with a consistent trading strategy that uses $100K balances and adapts in real time.
Speed is crucial in crypto trading, where opportunities can be fleeting. AI bots can execute trades in a fraction of a second, while human traders would take much longer to react. Platforms like 3Commas and CryptoHopper offer AI-powered bots that help traders implement complex strategies based on technical analysis or market sentiment. These bots work 24/7, capitalizing on price movements even when traders are offline.
Forbes discusses AI trading bots that automate 24/7 crypto trades with precision, speed, and improved risk management, enabling them to outperform manual trading. Automated strategies have also become more sophisticated. AI can now optimize these strategies in real time, adjusting buy and sell conditions as markets change. This level of flexibility makes automated trading more effective and profitable, even in unpredictable markets.
Crypto traders are no strangers to risk, especially given the market's infamous volatility. But the integration of AI into trading strategies is dramatically improving risk management techniques. With AI, traders can make more informed decisions to minimize their exposure to risk while optimizing their potential rewards.
One of the key benefits of AI is its ability to predict market volatility. By analyzing patterns from historical data and identifying early signs of market instability, AI can forecast potential market drops or surges. This allows traders to adjust their positions in real time, minimizing losses and maximizing gains.
AI also plays an essential role in enhancing the security of crypto trading platforms. Machine learning algorithms can detect unusual trading patterns that may indicate fraudulent activities, such as market manipulation or hacking attempts. By continuously monitoring transactions and identifying anomalies, AI can alert traders to potential threats before they cause damage.
Forbes explains how AI agents use predictive analytics and sentiment analysis to manage volatility and risks in crypto markets, reinforcing your points on AI-driven risk management. These advancements in risk management have made AI a crucial component of safe and effective trading, allowing both institutional and retail investors to navigate the crypto space with greater confidence.
While AI presents many benefits, its implementation in the crypto space is not without challenges and concerns. As more traders turn to AI to optimize their strategies, it’s essential to address potential risks and ethical issues associated with these technologies.
One significant issue with AI in trading is the risk of overfitting. Overfitting occurs when AI models become overly specialized in historical data, leading them to fail in volatile or unexpected market conditions. Traders who rely too heavily on these models may find their strategies backfire in uncharted territory.
As more traders use similar AI models, there’s a risk of herd behavior, where large groups of traders make identical decisions at the same time. This could amplify market instability, leading to bubbles or crashes. Ethical concerns also arise over whether AI systems could be used for market manipulation by those with the most advanced algorithms.
The rapid rise of AI in crypto trading has outpaced regulation. As AI systems become more autonomous, questions about accountability and transparency arise. Who is responsible if an AI bot makes a poor decision that causes significant losses? Regulatory bodies must evolve to ensure AI is used responsibly, providing clear guidelines for its integration into crypto markets.
As AI and machine learning continue to advance, their role in cryptocurrency trading will become increasingly significant. What does the future hold for AI in crypto?
The future of AI in crypto may involve deeper integration with blockchain technology. By combining the decentralized nature of blockchain with AI’s powerful data-processing capabilities, traders could achieve a new level of security, transparency, and efficiency in crypto trading.
AI will also play a key role in the growth of decentralized finance (DeFi). As DeFi protocols expand, AI can automate complex financial services, making them more accessible to a global audience. Forbes highlights that AI agents are driving automation and optimization in blockchain and DeFi. They are also supporting your view of AI's expanding role in decentralized finance.
For instance, AI can optimize lending, borrowing, and yield farming strategies on decentralized platforms, opening new avenues for digital asset investors. The continued evolution of AI promises to make crypto trading not just more accessible but also smarter, faster, and more secure.
Artificial Intelligence is no longer just a buzzword; it has become a crucial part of how traders approach cryptocurrency. By providing more accurate market predictions, automating complex strategies, and helping manage risks, AI is giving traders the tools they need to navigate a fast-moving, unpredictable market.
As AI continues to develop, it will only become more refined, helping traders make better, quicker decisions in a space that demands constant attention. Although still evolving, AI is already changing the game. Those who embrace it today will have a significant advantage tomorrow, making it an indispensable part of any serious crypto trading strategy.

articles.title: The Main Difference Between Algorithmic And AI Trading? Human Control
articles.query: site:forbes.com ("algorithmic trading" OR "AI trading" OR "quantitative trading" OR "robo-advisor")
articles.text:
Independent investors often use the terms "algorithmic trading" and "AI trading" interchangeably, but the two are actually completely different. One isn’t better than the other—in the same way that an SUV isn't objectively superior to a sports car. The type of vehicle you need depends on your lifestyle. And how you choose to implement algorithmic or AI trading tools depends on your individual investing goals.
Algorithmic trading is not a new concept. Financial institutions have been using algorithms for decades to make decisions more efficiently—and, more recently, retail traders have had more opportunities to leverage algorithms in their own investing strategies.
Algorithmic trading is a rule-based system where humans set the parameters in advance. It merges automation with human decision making and analysis. You instruct the algorithm to take actions based on specific triggers, including market indicators and mathematical formulas. For example: "When X happens in the market, then do Y."
You provide around 20% of the strategy and oversight, while the algorithm does the other 80% of the execution. The important thing is that you are always in charge. You make the rules. You know why the algorithm took a certain action, and you can monitor, adjust and stop it at any time.
AI trading , on the other hand, is a self-learning system that makes decisions based on past data. If an algorithm does around 80% of the work in a trade, then an AI system does closer to 99%. AI learns from past successes and failures, but the future is uncertain. External factors, such as tariffs, geopolitical crises and natural disasters, can change the market in an instant.
The fundamental difference between algorithmic and AI trading is control. With algorithmic trading, you maintain control. You can be adaptable and adjust your trading approach to dynamic conditions. With AI trading, you cede control. AI learns and develops its own patterns independently. If AI is in the driver’s seat, you don't know how it will react in an unpredictable situation. It may open or close a specific trade without you knowing why it took that particular action.
AI is still largely unproven at an institutional level because of its unpredictability. This doesn’t mean it lacks utility or potential. AI simply doesn't have the decades-long track record of algorithmic trading, and I believe many people are overestimating its current capabilities.
In 10 or 20 years, we may have incredible AI investing products that live up to their hype. But we’re not there yet. Influencers are selling a fantasy that AI will magically make you money without any effort on your part. This is one of the biggest misconceptions that I see within my company’s client base. People often don’t understand that automated trading software isn’t the same as AI operating on its own; it still depends on human strategy and analysis.
There is no such thing as a risk-free investment. Risk is universal in the market. Even the "safer" investments, such as treasury bonds or real estate, have variables that make them risky in some conditions. You could make a lot of money on a real estate investment—or you could lose a lot of money on that same investment at a different time. There are no guarantees.
Being an independent trader means you have to learn to manage your risk and make informed decisions—aiming to minimize your losses and make small, steady gains.
1. Model quality: AI software varies widely. One trading tool may be trained on more diverse data sets or be programmed with more nuance than another.
2. Market risk: An unforeseen event, such as a pandemic or a tariff war, could throw the market into a tailspin tomorrow. Humans can talk to experts, analyze data and try to understand what will happen next. AI is a wild card. We don’t know how AI will react in unpredictable circumstances.
3. Technical risk: Many of the most advanced AI tools available don’t offer transparency into how AI trains data or makes decisions. If you set rules for an algorithm, however, you decide how it will react in specific situations. You can build testing and quality assurance into the development process to fix errors and make improvements.
Understand the product you are buying and the promises it is making before you put any real money on the line. What can you do with algorithm trading right now? How much oversight and effort will it require from you to get the results you want? What is AI trading capable of right now? Are your expectations aligned with reality?
You may decide that you have $5,000 you want to test in AI trading, and you’re comfortable with the risks associated with it. That's fine. As long as you go in with eyes wide open, go for it.
I often tell investors: If you want to gamble, go to Las Vegas. At least if you lose money there, you can enjoy the lights and sights and sounds along the way. But why gamble with AI trading software? Where's the fun in watching your investment drop to zero by yourself in front of your computer? Be skeptical of any product that seems like a lot of smoke and mirrors. Take your time, do your due diligence and make responsible, step-by-step decisions that serve your individual investing goals.
